2608.01604.title: Post-Training on Office Work Improves Software Engineering: A Behavioral Account of Cross-Domain Transfer
2608.01604.paper_summary: Long-horizon tasks require agents to maintain coherent state and goals across nested and branching work. We call this capability goal-directed execution (GDE): the repeated application of four behaviors, namely selecting goals, constructing task-relevant state, maintaining fidelity to higher-level objectives, and verifying completion against the environment. We hypothesize that long-horizon post-training strengthens these behaviors across domains. We test this by post-training Qwen3.5-122B-A10B on 363 Long-Horizon Multi-Tool Agent (LHMTA) tasks drawn from office workflows. The collection contained no software-engineering tasks, yet the model's pass@1 improved by 5.8 points on SWE-Bench Pro. Matched trajectory analysis shows gains in all four GDE behaviors in both office workflows and software repositories. Aggregate SWE-Bench Pro statistics showed related changes in information gathering, implementation, and verification. Together, the results support a behavioral interpretation in which long-horizon post-training changed how the model organized and applied knowledge across tasks, with effects extending beyond the training domain.
2608.01604.paper_summary_zh: 長期任務要求代理在嵌套和分支工作中保持一致的狀態和目標。我們稱這種能力為目標導向執行（GDE）：即重複應用四種行為，即選擇目標、構建任務相關狀態、保持對高層目標的忠實度，以及根據環境驗證完成情況。我們假設長期後訓練會加強這些行為在不同領域的表現。我們通過對363個來自辦公室工作流程的長期多工具代理（LHMTA）任務進行Qwen3.5-122B-A10B的後訓練來測試這一假設。該集合不包含任何軟體工程任務，但模型在SWE-Bench Pro上的pass@1提高了5.8分。匹配軌跡分析顯示在辦公室工作流程和軟體庫中，所有四種GDE行為均有增長。綜合SWE-Bench Pro統計數據顯示在信息收集、實施和驗證方面的相關變化。綜合來看，結果支持一種行為解釋，即長期後訓練改變了模型在任務之間組織和應用知識的方式，影響超出了訓練領域。
